subject: Activation plan & eval gates for SailTech trial
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Willis <jack.willis@sailtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Activation plan & eval gates for SailTech trial

Hi Jack —

Following up from our demo: attached is a compact activation plan (redwood_map_v2.pdf) and the evaluation matrix (sailtech_eval_matrix.xlsx) that map the mutual action plan (MAP) to acceptance gates for the 2‑week trial. Key notes up front: 

- Proposed go/no‑go gates:
  1) Basic integration completeness (API auth + sample ingest) — target 2026‑10‑06
  2) Latency & throughput acceptance for critical endpoints (95th pct < 250ms) — target 2026‑10‑09
  3) Quality validation on representative prompt set (pass rate >= 90% on core flows) — target 2026‑10‑11
  4) Security/compliance evidence delivered (SOC scoping items) — target 2026‑10‑12

- Owners: SailTech to confirm internal owners for security and infra; Redwood owners are Ben (infra), Marissa (commercial/contract), and me (eng/ops).
- Blockers we anticipate: security evidence lag, staging data masking for evaluation, and an integration edge-case for streaming fallback.

Request: please confirm the SailTech owners and whether the gate dates look feasible. If you agree, I’ll publish a short weekly checkpoint cadence (Tue check-ins) and a shared action tracker.

Attachments: redwood_map_v2.pdf (MAP summary, 2 pages), sailtech_eval_matrix.xlsx (eval tests + scoring).

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0142
From: Jack Willis <jack.willis@sailtech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: SailTech POC Team <poc@sailtech.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Activation plan & eval gates for SailTech trial

Neha,

Thanks for the concise plan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Security owner: Laura Chen (laura.chen@sailtech.com) — she’ll lead evidence collection but is out until Tue (10/6). That likely pushes the security deliverable to 10/13 unless we can scope a minimal evidence bundle earlier.
- For the latency gate: our internal SLA window is 200ms for the UI path. Can you confirm whether the 250ms target you listed is conservative headroom or a fixed acceptance criteria?
- We have an internal data policy that requires staging data to be sanitized — we’ll need a short playbook from Redwood describing recommended masking approaches before we run the full quality set.

Also — would prefer a Wednesday checkpoint (our product sync is Tuesday evenings). Wednesday 10/7 at 10:00am ET works for us.

On the EV matrix: I’ll ask our engineering lead (cc’d) to mark any test cases that need additional context.

Jack
Head of Product, SailTech
jack.willis@sailtech.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Willis <jack.willis@sailtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@sailtech.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation plan & eval gates for SailTech trial

Jack / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and Laura’s note — understood on the scheduling and data mask requirement. Responses inline: 

- Latency target: 250ms was proposed as a pragmatic acceptance gate given cross‑region routing and batch behavior. We can tighten to 220ms for the UI path as a commercial acceptance if Redwood provides a short mitigation plan for the remaining tail (we’ll include a recommended batching/config profile and quantization suggestion in the MAP).

- Security evidence: agree minimal bundle to start (SOC scoping checklist + encryption/KMS attestation). Ben will own collecting and uploading the initial evidence set; estimate delivery 2026‑10‑12 given Laura’s return.

- Staging masking playbook: attached (see section 2.2 in redwood_map_v2.pdf) — it recommends a small anonymization script and sample config for our SDK. I’ll set a short tech‑deep dive with your infra lead if they want specifics before running the full quality set.

- Checkpoint moved to Wed 10/7 10:00am ET — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Action items captured (owner / due):
- Provide minimal security evidence bundle (Ben / 2026‑10‑12)
- Publish sanitized staging playbook and sample script (Neha / 2026‑10‑05) — attached
- Confirm latency acceptance for UI path as 220ms (Jack / 2026‑10‑06)
- Mark eval cases needing extra context in matrix (SailTech Eng / 2026‑10‑06)
- Contract tweak (Marissa to propose small DocuSign amendment for trial obligation / 2026‑10‑08)

Attachments referenced: redwood_map_v2.pdf (updated), sailtech_eval_matrix.xlsx (awaiting flags).

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jack Willis <jack.willis@sailtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2026 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation plan & eval gates for SailTech trial — security evidence upload

Quick update from infra: we uploaded the initial evidence bundle to the shared folder (link in the MAP doc and short list below).

Uploaded items:
- SOC scoping checklist (partial)
- KMS attestation snapshot (key IDs redacted)
- TLS cert chain and endpoint scanning summary

Outstanding blocker: we still need SailTech to confirm whether they can accept the partial SOC scoping for the purposes of the trial, or if they require the full control matrix. If SailTech needs the full matrix, timing slips to 10/15.

Next internal steps: Marissa will publish the trial amendment and I’ll stand by to provide any extra environment logs the security team asks for.

Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thread notes (internal summary compiled by Neha):
- Weekly cadence: Wednesdays at 10:00am ET, next sync 2026‑10‑07 (invite sent).
- Current gating status entering the second week: integration done; infra evidence uploaded; latency tuning in progress; awaiting SailTech confirmation on UI latency acceptance and eval flags.
- Open blockers: acceptance on partial security deliverable (SailTech decision), and finalization of a small streaming fallback test case flagged in the eval matrix.
- Next publish: final MAP snapshot (redwood_map_v2.pdf) with updated gates and a one‑page escalation path if acceptance slips beyond 10/15.
